subject: Regionalization safeguards & VPC peering acceptance - action items
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@axiombank.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: infra-team@axiombank.com
Date: 2026-11-09 07:12:00 +0000
Subject: Regionalization plan & VPC peering acceptance (EU/APAC)

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks again for the briefing yesterday. As we scope our private deployment for AxiomBank, legal has asked for a concise set of technical acceptance criteria we can sign off on for EU -> APAC warm-standby peering and egress containment. In particular we need: 

- A checklist for network ACLs and peering controls that ensure no accidental cross-border egress during failover.
- Requirements for KMS key locality and proof-of-possession during resident-mode operations.
- A short runbook describing the failover trigger, cutover steps, and rollback criteria that our network team can run in a tabletop.

I've attached our internal summary of regulatory must-haves (axiom_peering_requirements.pdf). Can Redwood provide a single-sheet acceptance checklist and an example sim plan we could run with your ops?

We'd like to schedule a tabletop the week of Nov 22 if possible. Please confirm owners and any pre-work.

Thanks,
Alex Chen
Lead Infrastructure Architect
AxiomBank

Attachments: axiom_peering_requirements.pdf (PDF, 294 KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@axiombank.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-09 10:03:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Regionalization plan & VPC peering acceptance (EU/APAC)

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. Quick response with next steps and the artifacts we'll produce before the tabletop: 

1) Acceptance checklist (one page): VPC peering ACLs, egress lock policies, control-plane endpoints and allowed CIDR scopes, KMS jurisdiction checks, and SLOs for control-plane convergence.
2) Technical runbook (playbook): step-by-step failover procedure, validation probes, and rollback criteria.
3) Tabletop simulation plan: roles, injects, expected telemetry, and a postmortem template.

I've attached our baseline checklist (redwood_peering-checklist.xlsx) and a draft sim plan (controlplane-sim-plan.docx). Please ask your infra team to confirm their BGP/eBGP peering window as well as any private interconnect (Equinix/Carrier) maintenance constraints.

For the KMS requests: Redwood supports customer-managed keys with regional binding for private deployments. We'll include the KMS locality proof we keep in our attestation package, and we'll map the key usage to the resident cluster in the checklist.

Proposed owners:
- Redwood tech lead / tabletop: Marissa Cole
- Redwood network & peering lead: Ben Carter
- Axiom lead for BGP/peering: Alex Chen

Can Marissa confirm she can run the tabletop on Nov 23 (UTC-friendly time)? If not, Nov 24.

Thanks,
Karthik
Customer Solutions Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_peering-checklist.xlsx (Excel, 76 KB), controlplane-sim-plan.docx (Word, 48 KB)

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@axiombank.com>, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2026-11-09 14:22:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Regionalization plan & VPC peering acceptance (EU/APAC)

Alex — happy to run the tabletop. A couple of clarifications I want captured in the pre-work so the simulation is productive: 

- Egress containment modes: are you expecting hard-block egress (drop) at the egress gateway layer, or do you want graceful drain that routes to a quarantined EU-only egress? We should test both flows.
- Control-plane split behavior: in warm-standby we keep the control plane passive in APAC until a region-declared failover. We'll validate leader election and KV-store reconciliation during the injects.
- KMS: if you require key material never leave EU, we'll validate signing and crypto operations inside the EU-resident enclave and produce an attestation trace for the test.

Pre-work items for Axiom infra team: 
1) Updated BGP peer list and expected ASN changes during the failover window.
2) Confirmation of private interconnect / colo fiber availability on proposed dates.
3) A list of critical routing prefixes to monitor for accidental propagation.

If those are in place I can allocate 2 hours for the tabletop plus 1 hour for the postmortem readout. Nov 23 at 13:00 UTC works for our ops leads. 

Ben — can you prepare the network ACL snippets we will validate (both GCP/Azure style and on-prem firewall ACL examples)? Vivek — we'll need the attestation artifacts for KMS locality.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Architect, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redwood_peering-checklist.xlsx, controlplane-sim-plan.docx

Date: 2026-11-10 16:48:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: Regionalization plan & VPC peering acceptance (EU/APAC)

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect. A few follow-ups: 

- We'll aim to provide the BGP peer list and prefix inventory by Nov 17.
- Legal has asked for a short Data Processing Addendum (DPA) appendix describing the peering behavior and failover guarantees. Can your contracts team produce a one-page appendix?
- For the KMS attestation, can Redwood produce an example artifact (signed) ahead of the tabletop so our auditors can confirm the format?

We'll take Nov 23 13:00 UTC. Please send calendar invite and the runbook version you'd like us to pre-load. I'll mark infra-team@axiombank.com as owners for pre-work.

Regards,
Alex

--
Alex Chen
Lead Infrastructure Architect
AxiomBank

Attachments: none
